title: Sonos Error 100 - Unable to Connect
shortDescription: The Sonos app cannot establish a connection to the sound bar during setup or playback.
fullDescription:
Sonos error 100 indicates a general connection failure between the Sonos app and the sound bar. It appears during initial setup, firmware updates, or when the app tries to communicate with a previously paired speaker.

This error is most often caused by network issues such as router isolation, IGMP snooping, or a mismatch between the phone's WiFi network and the speaker's network. Temporary Sonos cloud outages can also trigger it.

Restarting the sound bar, the router, and the Sonos app usually resolves the issue. Persistent failures may require network configuration changes on the router.

causes.cause: Phone and sound bar on different WiFi networks or bands
Router blocking multicast or SSDP traffic

symptoms: Speaker greyed out in Rooms list

fixSteps.title: Reboot sound bar and router
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug the sound bar and router for 60 seconds, then power on the router first, wait 2 minutes, then the sound bar.

fixSteps.title: Check WiFi network
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure your phone is on the same 2.4GHz or 5GHz network as the sound bar. Disable cellular data temporarily.

fixSteps.title: Disable router AP isolation
fixSteps.instruction: Log into your router admin page and turn off AP/client isolation, enable IGMP snooping, and enable UPnP.

whenToCallPro: Call a network technician if router settings cannot be adjusted or if multiple Sonos devices fail simultaneously.

faq.q: Does Error 100 mean my sound bar is broken?
faq.a: No, it is almost always a network or app connection issue.
Only after rebooting and adjusting router settings fail.

title: Sonos Error 101 - Firmware Mismatch
shortDescription: The sound bar firmware is out of date and cannot sync with the Sonos system.
fullDescription:
Error 101 occurs when the sound bar's firmware version does not match other Sonos devices on the system or the minimum version required by the current Sonos app.

This is common after moving a speaker from another household, after long periods offline, or when the S1/S2 controller mismatch arises.

Updating the firmware from the Sonos app normally clears the error. In S1/S2 cases, users must choose the correct controller app for their hardware.

fixSteps.title: Update firmware
fixSteps.instruction: Open the Sonos app, go to Settings > System > System Updates and run the update.

fixSteps.title: Verify controller
fixSteps.instruction: Older sound bars need S1; newer ones need S2. Download the right app.

whenToCallPro: Only call support if firmware update fails repeatedly.

faq.a: Check sonos.com/swgen for S1 vs S2 compatibility.

title: Sonos Error 102 - Update Failed
fullDescription:
Error 102 occurs when a firmware update to the Sonos sound bar is interrupted, typically by a network disconnect or power loss.

The sound bar may end up in a partially updated state, refusing to play audio until the update is successfully reapplied.

Re-running the update from a stable wired Ethernet connection usually resolves the issue.

fixSteps.title: Use wired Ethernet
fixSteps.instruction: Connect the sound bar to the router via Ethernet cable during update.

fixSteps.title: Retry update
fixSteps.instruction: Run Settings > System > System Updates in the Sonos app.

whenToCallPro: Contact Sonos if updates continue failing on wired Ethernet.

faq.a: No, partially updated units require a successful update to function.

title: Sonos Error 901 - Music Service Unavailable
shortDescription: A streaming service failed to authenticate with the Sonos sound bar.
fullDescription:
Error 901 appears when a music service (Spotify, Apple Music, Amazon Music, etc.) cannot complete authentication on the Sonos sound bar.

The cause is typically an expired OAuth token, account-sharing limits, or a temporary service outage. Re-linking the account in the Sonos app clears the error.

fixSteps.title: Re-link service
fixSteps.instruction: In the Sonos app go to Settings > Services & Voice, remove the service, and add it again.

fixSteps.title: Check service status
fixSteps.instruction: Verify the streaming service is online via its status page.

whenToCallPro: Rarely needed; contact streaming service support if re-linking fails.

faq.q: Why does this happen after months?
faq.a: OAuth tokens periodically expire and need renewal.

title: Sonos Error 913 - Unable to Browse Service
shortDescription: The sound bar cannot load browse data from a streaming service.
fullDescription:
Error 913 is shown when the Sonos sound bar fails to retrieve catalog/browse data from a configured music service.

The issue is usually a temporary service glitch, but may also stem from DNS problems on the local network or a region restriction.

fixSteps.title: Reboot router
fixSteps.instruction: Restart the router to refresh DNS and reconnect the sound bar.

fixSteps.title: Change DNS
fixSteps.instruction: Set router DNS to 8.8.8.8 and 1.1.1.1 if the issue persists.

whenToCallPro: Contact ISP if DNS issues persist across devices.

faq.q: Is this my Sonos or the service?
faq.a: Usually the service; check its status page first.

title: Sonos Error 1002 - Cannot Play Track
shortDescription: The sound bar cannot play the selected track.
fullDescription:
Error 1002 occurs when a specific track cannot be played, often because it is unavailable in your region, has been removed from the streaming service, or the file format is unsupported.

Skipping the track or re-selecting from a different source usually bypasses the error.

fixSteps.title: Skip track
fixSteps.instruction: Tap skip to move to the next track.

fixSteps.title: Re-index library
fixSteps.instruction: For NAS libraries, go to Settings > System > Music Library and re-index.

title: Sonos HDMI ARC Error
shortDescription: Sound bar cannot establish an HDMI ARC connection with the TV.
fullDescription:
The Sonos Arc, Beam, and Ray rely on HDMI ARC/eARC for TV audio. An ARC error means either the cable, TV port, or CEC settings are misconfigured.

Many TVs disable ARC by default or label the ARC port (HDMI 2 or 3). Without correct CEC settings, the sound bar cannot receive audio from the TV.
symptoms: TV audio reverts to TV speakers

fixSteps.title: Use ARC/eARC port
fixSteps.instruction: Plug HDMI cable into the port labeled ARC or eARC on your TV.

fixSteps.title: Enable CEC
fixSteps.instruction: In TV settings, enable HDMI-CEC (varies by brand).

fixSteps.title: Replace HDMI cable
fixSteps.instruction: Use a high-speed HDMI cable certified for ARC/eARC.

whenToCallPro: If the HDMI port on the TV is damaged or CEC menu is missing.

faq.a: eARC is required for lossless Dolby Atmos via TrueHD.

title: Sonos Sound Bar WiFi Error
shortDescription: The sound bar cannot connect to WiFi.
fullDescription:
A WiFi error indicates the sound bar cannot associate with or authenticate to your wireless router.

Common causes include incorrect password, unsupported security type (WPA3-only), or weak signal near the sound bar's location.

fixSteps.title: Re-enter WiFi credentials
fixSteps.instruction: Use Settings > System > Networks in the Sonos app.

fixSteps.title: Enable WPA2 compatibility
fixSteps.instruction: On the router, switch security to WPA2 or WPA2/WPA3 mixed mode.

whenToCallPro: If signal boosters are needed in the room.
videoSearchQuery: Sonos sound bar WiFi error fix

faq.a: Newer Sonos products support WPA3, older ones require WPA2.

title: Sonos Unable to Connect to Speaker
shortDescription: The app cannot reach a previously set up sound bar.
fullDescription: This generic connection error usually appears on the Rooms screen. The app and sound bar are on the same network but cannot communicate, often due to mDNS/SSDP blockage or DHCP lease changes.

fixSteps.title: Force-close Sonos app
fixSteps.instruction: Swipe the app away and reopen.

fixSteps.title: Reserve DHCP IP
fixSteps.instruction: In router settings, reserve a static IP for the sound bar.

whenToCallPro: Rare unless network requires advanced configuration.
videoSearchQuery: Sonos unable to connect speaker fix

title: Sonos Speaker Offline
shortDescription: The sound bar shows as offline in the Sonos app.
fullDescription:
An offline sound bar has lost its network registration. It may still be powered on but no longer communicating with the Sonos cloud.

Power cycling the unit and router usually restores it. Mesh WiFi handoffs are a common culprit.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug the sound bar for 30 seconds and plug back in.

faq.a: No, settings are stored in your account.

title: Sonos Firmware Update Failed
shortDescription: The firmware update process terminated with an error.
fullDescription: A failed firmware update leaves the sound bar in a pending-update state. It usually retries automatically, but a manual rerun after stabilizing the network is recommended.

causes.cause: Insufficient flash space due to bug

fixSteps.title: Wired Ethernet
fixSteps.instruction: Connect via Ethernet and retry the update.

fixSteps.title: Factory reset
fixSteps.instruction: Hold join/Bluetooth button while powering on to reset.

whenToCallPro: If unit is bricked after update.

faq.a: Usually no; a reset and retry restores it.

title: Sonos Trueplay Tuning Error
fullDescription: Trueplay uses the iPhone microphone to measure room acoustics. Errors happen when ambient noise is too high, the phone microphone is muted, or an Android device is used (Trueplay is iOS-only for traditional tuning).

fixSteps.title: Silence the room
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off fans, HVAC, and close windows.

fixSteps.title: Grant mic permission
fixSteps.instruction: Allow Sonos app microphone access in iOS settings.

fixSteps.title: Use an iOS device
fixSteps.instruction: Borrow an iPhone or iPad for Trueplay setup.

faq.q: Can I run Trueplay on Android?
faq.a: Only the newer Quick Tune is available on Android; traditional Trueplay is iOS only.
